title: Admin override: suppress auto-rollback with audited justification
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary: Adds admin-only override APIs to temporarily suppress auto actions (auto-pause/auto-rollback) for a specific rollout or for a broader service scope, with required justification captured in the rollout audit trail. This is intended for incident response and known-incident/telemetry-outage scenarios to avoid oscillation or false positives while teams investigate. Motivation: During game-day and the 2026-02-17 simulation we saw cases where monitors were stale/lagged and the controller behavior (fail-safe pauses) caused repeated halts. SRE asked for an explicit, auditable suppression lever gated by RBAC (see INT-8832) that does not require editing rollout policies mid-incident. Design notes: Suppressions are stored as TTL-based records in the control plane (new table + service layer). The rollout controller consults suppressions during SLO evaluation; if a suppression matches, it emits a 'decision=suppress' audit event and surfaces the suppression reason in the decision trace. The API requires a human-readable justification and duration; duration is bounded to prevent indefinite suppressions. This aligns with ADR-0128 audit requirements (actor, policy_version, monitor refs, reason, TTL). API surface: POST /v1/admin/rollouts/{rollout_id}/auto-actions/suppress (rollout-scoped suppression); POST /v1/admin/services/{service}/auto-actions/suppress (service-scoped suppression; optional route/model/region/tier selectors); DELETE /v1/admin/auto-actions/suppressions/{suppression_id} (lift early); GET /v1/admin/auto-actions/suppressions?rollout_id=...&service=... (list active). All endpoints are behind RBAC permission rollouts.auto_actions.override and require X-Redwood-Admin-Justification header (duplicated into request body for audit durability). Guardrails: suppression_duration_seconds min=300, max=86400 (24h); justification min length 15; a suppression cannot be created if no matching rollout/service scope exists (prevents typos creating dead records); lifting a suppression also produces an audit event. Auditability: emits rollouts.audit_event with action=auto_action_suppression_created|auto_action_suppression_lifted and includes suppression_id, scope, created_by, expires_at, justification, and correlation_id. Controller emits decision trace with suppression_id when suppression prevents an action (no rollback executor call is made). Backward compatibility: No change to existing policy schema. The override is an orthogonal layer with higher precedence than policy actions (suppression wins). Feature flag: rollouts.autoActions.adminOverride.enabled (default off in prod; on in dev/staging). Follow-ups: Console UI will consume the list endpoint in ENG-4833; incident-bot formatting will be updated separately to include suppression state when relevant. Testing: Unit tests for RBAC enforcement, TTL expiry behavior, scope matching, and audit event payload; integration test that a suppressed rollout emits 'decision=suppress' and does not call rollback executor; added negative tests for missing/short justification and out-of-bounds duration. Risk/mitigation: The primary risk is abuse/misuse during incidents; mitigated via admin-only RBAC, required justification, time bounds, and audit trail. Also added rate limiting (server-side) to 10 suppression mutations/min per actor to avoid accidental loops.
commits: control-plane: add AutoActionSuppression model + TTL index
api: admin endpoints for create/list/delete suppressions
rollout-controller: consult suppression store before executing auto action
audit: emit suppression created/lifted + suppression-hit decision trace
tests: unit + integration coverage for suppression matching and expiry
test_plan: manual: create rollout-scoped suppression; verify controller emits decision=suppress and rollout continues without auto action
review_conversation:
Chloe Martin: Can we confirm these endpoints are truly admin-only and not accidentally exposed via the public Console API gateway? Also prefer consistent naming with existing /v1/admin/* routes.
Benji Okafor: Yes, these are on the admin router only (same as existing admin backfills). Renamed path to /v1/admin/... and added an explicit gateway denylist entry for non-admin.

Sean Gallagher: Please cap suppression duration. We cannot have indefinite suppressions lingering post-incident. Also want the controller to emit a metric/audit when suppression prevents a rollback so oncall has breadcrumbs.
Benji Okafor: Added max=24h, min=5m; controller emits audit event with decision=suppress and includes suppression_id + expires_at. Metric wiring will come with ENG-4840/ENG-4837.

Kevin Osei: Justification must be mandatory and captured immutably in audit log. Also ensure PII guidance is in the error message.
Benji Okafor: Made justification required in header and body; audit event stores the body copy. Updated validation errors to include 'Do not include customer PII' hint and added tests.

Jordan Lee: Scope matching rules need to be deterministic (especially when service-level suppression + rollout-level suppression both exist). Document precedence.
Benji Okafor: Documented precedence (rollout-level > service-level; both override policy) in code comments + added tests.

Jada Williams: The evaluator currently short-circuits on suppression but we should still record the SLO snapshot for later analysis.
Benji Okafor: Agreed; we still fetch the SLO status but do not execute actions; decision trace includes monitor ids + timestamp and suppression_id.

release_notes: Added admin-only API to suppress auto-rollback/auto-pause for a rollout or service scope for a bounded duration with mandatory justification.
Controller records suppression-hit decisions in audit trail for incident forensics.
